excerpt: Al-Fanar Media, in partnership with Effat University, is holding a workshop on “Media Literacy and Fact-Checking Basics” for Saudi students at the university’s campus in Jeddah this week. The free workshop, which runs from Sunday to Thursday, aims to strengthen media literacy among Saudi university students. Conducted in English, the workshop focuses on developing critical thinking skills to help students assess media content, distinguish between reliable and misleading information, and engage with media reports in an informed and responsible way. Mirna Abou Zeid, dean of the Jordan Media Institute and a specialist in media literacy and fact-checking, is leading the workshop, with help from Josette Abi Tamer, a digital investigative journalist, fact-checking trainer, and lecturer in digital journalism at the Lebanese American University. Media Literacy This workshop is part of a Media Literacy Project that Al-Fanar Media has been conducting over the past 18 months with support from the New York-based Ford Foundation. The initiative aims to educate university students across the Arab world to engage thoughtfully and critically with media content and strengthen their skills in verifying whether information is trustworthy—skills that are particularly relevant in light of the growth of misinformation and AI-generated fake content. Al-Fanar Media has run workshops in several Arab countries in collaboration with leading academic institutions. These training sessions cover topics such as the traits of trustworthy journalism, navigating information disruption in the digital age, identifying fake news and media misinformation, understanding deepfakes, and developing skills to verify published content and digital sources. Haifa Reda Jamal Al-Lail, president of Effat University, said it was essential that educational institutions provide media literacy training. “Media literacy may be the most important form of knowledge in our world today,” Jamal Al-Lail said. “Media messages surround us, and their impact on our lives is significant. Mastering media and digital skills is not a luxury, but a necessity to protect individuals and empower them as active citizens.” She added that through this collaboration, Effat University was trying to prepare leaders who can offer solutions to the challenges society is facing and drive progress. Dangers of Misinformation Mohammad El-Hawary, chief executive and editor-in-chief of Al-Fanar Media, stressed the dangers posed by the spread of misinformation and disinformation. “What we’ve witnessed over the years reveals the serious impact of fake news, disinformation, and media instability—alongside the rise of hate speech, racism, distortion of facts, and the manipulation of truth to serve specific agendas,” El-Hawary said. “These forces contribute to societal fragility, division, and even the collapse of states.” El-Hawary said Al-Fanar Media was committed to helping young Arabs learn to think analytically, evaluate media content, and learn fact-checking skills, while supporting universities and their students across all disciplines, not just media. “We believe that media and information literacy are essential skills, especially in the age of artificial intelligence,” he said. “These skills help strengthen the capacities of younger generations and foster a culture of fact-checking, creating informed, responsible citizens who can support social unity and cohesion.” El-Hawary thanked Effat University for
